caption: The drawing depicts a small outdoor porch or veranda, accessed by a short staircase with six beige stone steps, and flanked by green railings at the stairs' sides. The porch is surrounded by ornate, decorative wrought iron railings and supports, all painted green. Above the porch and to the right, intricate scrollwork and patterns in the same green color form an elaborate overhead structure. Draped around and over the porch structure are abundant vines and clusters of wisteria flowers in shades of purple, lavender, and pink, with green leaves interspersed throughout. Some flowers and foliage cascade downward, partially covering the railings and the top of the veranda. Behind the open space of the porch, faint watercolor-like indications of a building wall and a large rectangular door or window are visible, rendered in light shades of blue, grey, and beige. At the very bottom, the drawing also suggests two small windows beneath the porch. The background is left uncolored, with the paper’s natural tone serving as the backdrop.
title: Cast Iron Porch Railing
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
